title: Upstream hexane/src/tests.rs case ledger: every #[test] occurrence and the Zig declaration that asserts it

method.instrument: Every byte of the reference is classified as code, comment or literal; attribute spans are matched in code only with balanced brackets; each #[test] span binds to the next fn declaration in code order. One-to-one: 286 spans, 286 distinct fn targets, no collision and no orphan.
method.status_rule: covered = a Zig declaration asserts upstream's values, operations and refusals for that occurrence. excluded = one of two things, and each exclusion record says which: either the reference does not run the case in its default build - 13 of the 14, being the nine under #[cfg(feature = "bijou64")], the three under cfg_attr(not(feature = "deep_fuzz"), ignore) and the one #[ignore]d benchmark that asserts nothing - or the case's whole obligation is a Rust-only trait this port has no notion of, which is one: load_with_opts_is_copy, which the reference does run and whose body is a #[derive(Copy)] check. There is no partial and no missing case in this tree, and no record is covered on a name match alone.
method.not_name_presence: A matching test name is not by itself coverage. Where no declaration carries the name, zig.sub is true and names the declaration that asserts the case instead. Where an excluded occurrence shares a name with a declaration over the port's own codec, that declaration is parked under same_name and is never counted.
method.verified: read = this ledger's author read the declaration's body against this tree. digest = the block's assertion calls were extracted and recorded; the reader can audit any record from zig.digest and the line range.
method.anchors: zig.line is a snapshot of the tree at 2026-10-04; the durable anchor is zig.t, the Zig test name. attr, decl and body are the reference's lines and are pinned by the commit above.
method.source_frozen: Anchors were re-derived against the final frozen source on 2026-10-04. Column.encode now keeps the true/false tail value when equal boolean runs merge; a standalone merged count cannot recover that value without the column run parity (rust/hexane/src/bool.rs:855-857). The exhaustive boolean splice case failed before this repair and passes afterward. The eight integration cases retain their assertions; expectCanonical now reports splice coordinates on encoder refusal. Bool module documentation names the actual root route, zautomerge.hexane.bool_codec. All 272 covered declarations resolve. Production edits did not change the recorded test assertion digests.

duplicated_names.note: ids are module-qualified; a lookup by bare name returns two rows for each of these, on purpose

resolved_since_the_previous_revision: mod alt_codec is ungated upstream (tests.rs:5412) and its five cases are covered. BeLen reaches PrefixBase, RleBase (nullable and plain), BoolCodec, DeltaBase and the delta module's own writer. prefix_column holds the byte divergence at tests.rs:5487; u64_column_roundtrip_and_wire_divergence holds all four of its assertions including the cross-codec load at 5506-5507; delta_column holds all three; splice_and_nullable holds both; string_and_bool_columns holds exactly the two same-codec load equalities upstream has - there is no assert_ne! in that case, and an earlier revision of this ledger wrongly claimed one because it inherited the port's own in-case comment.

The packed literal-header fixture added to splice_and_nullable was repaired. It previously drove a load at a budget of three over seven distinct values and asserted cut.slabCount() > 1, which is false: seven distinct values canonicalise to one literal run, so the column was one slab. It now builds two individually canonical BeLen literal slabs in a real Column, reindexes and rebuilds the aggregates, asserts exactly two slabs and expectSound, then encodes and load/row-checks the joined bytes. Upstream's two assertions are untouched at the top of the declaration.

nullable_basic's header cited tests.rs:166, :173, :180, :187 - which are build_with_repeats, build_all_same, get_in_bounds and remove_middle - and claimed upstream has a fourth, string, case and that the port has no byte-string codec. Both were false. The header now reads 'Nullable insertion preserves row order (tests.rs:192-199)' and sits inside the declaration's braces, which is upstream's case exactly and what AGENTS requires.

cross_slab_fuzz_regression now replays a recorded trace from test/golden/hexane-regression.jsonl, drawn by tools/oracle's hexane-regression subcommand from upstream's own SmallRng and the reference's own Column<u64> answers, and compares rows and canonical bytes after every step.

cross_slab_fuzz is an RLE column at a 3..=8 run budget, not the byte arena; the arena sweep is re-homed under the port-only name byte_arena_cross_slab_fuzz so name-presence cannot score it as upstream's case.

On a 64-bit target rand's SmallRng and Zig's DefaultPrng are the same generator, Xoshiro256++. They part before the first draw - rand_core expands a u64 seed with PCG32, Zig with SplitMix64 - and at the bounded reduction per draw. The earlier in-tree claim that they are different generators has been corrected in raw.zig, slab.zig and prefix.zig.

The two declarations that wore gated upstream names are renamed: save_load_save_is_identity is now re_encoding_after_a_load_returns_the_same_bytes and string_bool_delta_prefix_columns is now one_fixture_through_the_text_boolean_delta_and_prefix_codecs, so name-presence cannot score the two bijou64 occurrences.
fuzz_splice_ops and fuzz_sequential_splice_uint are real declarations rather than one invented substitute; splice_matches_a_model and oneSweep are deleted.
The comment claiming a consumer can reach none of the packed factories is narrowed: BeLen and the column factories are private, and the public rle, bool and delta seams are named honestly.
